Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves, puckered or distorted leaf surfaces.
Apple___Apple_scab.management: Rake and destroy fallen leaves to reduce overwintering fungi. Apply preventive fungicides during early spring bud break. Choose scab-resistant apple cultivars.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Frog-eye leaf spots (circular brown spots with purple margins), stem cankers, and mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.management: Prune out dead wood and mummified apples. Disinfect pruning shears between cuts. Ensure good canopy airflow.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish spots on upper leaf surfaces, tube-like fungal aecia underneath.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.management: Remove nearby red cedar or juniper alternate hosts if possible. Apply protective fungicidal sprays at blossom stage.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are vibrant green with smooth edges and no visible lesions or chlorosis.
Apple___healthy.management: Continue standard orchard nutrition, adequate watering, and routine pest scouting.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Firm, evenly colored green leaves without spotting, wilting, or yellowing veins.
Blueberry___healthy.management: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5–5.5), mulch with pine bark or peat moss, and irrigate regularly.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White to light gray powdery fungal patches on young leaves, curling or leaf distortion.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.management: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation. Prune dense branches to enhance sunlight penetration. Apply sulfur or horticultural oil sprays.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant foliage free of mold, yellowing, or necrotic punctures.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.management: Ensure balanced nitrogen fertilization and regular monitoring during warm, humid weather.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.disease: Cercospora Leaf Spot / Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular, tan to gray lesions running parallel to leaf veins, blighting large leaf sections.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.management: Rotate crops with non-grasses like soybeans. Use disease-tolerant corn hybrids. Practice residue management.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, powdery cinnamon-brown to dark-red pustules scattered across both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.management: Plant rust-resistant hybrids. In severe early infestations, apply labeled foliar fungicides.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions that eventually turn papery and necrotic.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.management: Select resistant hybrids with Ht genes. Implement crop rotation and tillage to bury infected crop residue.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Strong, erect green blades without streaks, pustules, or blotches.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.management: Maintain proper plant spacing, balanced NPK fertilizer, and adequate soil moisture.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small, circular reddish-brown leaf spots with tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) inside.
Grape___Black_rot.management: Prune out infected canes and mummified grape clusters during dormancy. Apply protective fungicides before bloom.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Interveinal tiger-stripe discoloration (yellowing and browning between veins) on leaves.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).management: Minimize large pruning wounds during wet weather. Remove severely infected vines to avoid spreading spores.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown patches on foliage, causing premature defoliation in late summer.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.management: Ensure adequate trellis ventilation. Apply copper-based or systemic fungicides after petal fall.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Broad, dark green foliage with healthy vein networks and no necrotic spotting.
Grape___healthy.management: Support vines on sturdy trellises, manage canopy density, and inspect periodically.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterial (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, spread by psyllid insect)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy yellow mottle on leaves, small lopsided bitter fruit, leaf vein corking.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).management: Control Asian citrus psyllid vector populations. Remove infected trees promptly. Use certified disease-free nursery stock.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked polygonal angular spots on leaves turning purple-brown, leading to shot-holes.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.management: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization. Apply preventive copper or oxytetracycline sprays in early season.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Long, lanceolate green leaves without perforated holes or chlorotic edges.
Peach___healthy.management: Prune annually for sunlight penetration and mulch root zone to conserve soil moisture.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn dark brown with yellowish haloes, causing leaf drop.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.management: Use certified clean seed. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation. Apply copper fungicides combined with mancozeb.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Smooth, glossy green leaves with intact margins and firm plant stems.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.management: Maintain consistent watering to avoid blossom end rot; apply balanced vegetable fertilizers.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric rings forming a 'target-board' pattern in dark brown spots on older lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.management: Practice 3-year crop rotation. Mulch soil to prevent rain splash. Apply chlorothalonil or copper-based sprays.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark water-soaked lesions on leaves with white fuzzy fungal growth on the underside during high humidity.
Potato___Late_blight.management: Destroy volunteer potato tubers. Plant certified blight-free seed potatoes. Spray preventive fungicides immediately upon weather warnings.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Compound leaves showing vibrant green pigmentation with no concentric rings or water-soaked margins.
Potato___healthy.management: Hill up soil around stems, maintain steady irrigation, and monitor for Colorado potato beetles.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Serrated green leaves with distinct veins and no signs of cane blight or rust.
Raspberry___healthy.management: Prune old floricanes after harvest, ensure well-draining organic soil, and stake canes for airflow.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves exhibiting uniform green coloration without rust pustules or bacterial blighting.
Soybean___healthy.management: Rotate with corn, ensure adequate nodulation/inoculation, and monitor weed competition.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Talcum powder-like white spots that expand to cover entire leaf surfaces, causing leaves to yellow and dry.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.management: Plant in full sunlight with wide spacing. Use mildew-tolerant varieties. Spray neem oil, sulfur, or potassium bicarbonate.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Irregular purple or dark reddish spots that coalesce, giving leaves a scorched, burnt appearance.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.management: Remove and discard dead leaves in autumn. Plant in raised beds to ensure good drainage. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Low-growing lush green leaves with serrated margins and no purplish blotches.
Strawberry___healthy.management: Apply straw mulch around crowns to keep fruit and leaves off bare wet soil.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy or water-soaked spots with yellow rings; leaves yellow and drop prematurely.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.management: Sanitize stakes and cages. Avoid working with wet plants. Apply copper bactericides early.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('bullseye' appearance) surrounded by yellow chlorotic halos.
Tomato___Early_blight.management: Remove lower infected foliage. Stake plants to keep leaves off soil. Mulch heavily and apply preventive fungicides.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular oily dark green to brown lesions with white downy growth on leaf undersides in cool, wet weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.management: Remove and bag infected plants immediately. Avoid overhead watering. Choose late blight-resistant tomato cultivars.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green or yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces; olive-green velvety mold coating underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.management: Maximize ventilation in greenhouses and high tunnels. Keep relative humidity below 85%.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with grayish-white centers and dark brown borders; tiny black dots in centers.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.management: Prune lowest branches 12 inches above soil. Rotate tomatoes with non-solanaceous crops. Mulch base.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or bronzing on leaves, accompanied by delicate silk webbing on leaf undersides.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.management: Spray with insecticidal soap or horticultural oil. Introduce predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis). Increase humidity.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small brown spots that enlarge into zoned circular lesions with light brown centers.
Tomato___Target_Spot.management: Improve air circulation around canopy. Avoid wetting leaves during irrigation. Apply labeled broad-spectrum fungicides.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Stunted bushy growth, upward curling or cupping of leaves, prominent interveinal chlorosis.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.management: Manage whitefly vectors with yellow sticky traps and insecticidal soap. Use TYLCV-resistant hybrids.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on foliage, distorted 'shoestring' or fern-like leaves.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.management: Wash hands with milk or soap before handling plants (tobacco users take extra care). Disinfect tools. Plant resistant varieties.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Crisp, deep green leaves with no lesions, curling, stippling, or mold.
Tomato___healthy.management: Provide regular deep watering at the base, feed with balanced tomato food, and prune suckers for optimal airflow.
